and Voicebox, despite its extremely simple framework.
Table 2 illustrated the subjective evaluation results for Natural-
Speech 3, Voicebox, and E2 TTS. Firstly, all variants of E2 TTS,
from (P1) to (P3), showed a better CMOS score compared to Natu-
ralSpeech 3 and Voicebox. In particular, the (P2) model achieved a
CMOS score of -0.05, which is considered to have a level of natural-
ness indistinguishable from the ground truth [15, 24].7 The compar-
ison between (B4) and (P1) suggests that the use of phoneme align-
ment was the major bottleneck in achieving better naturalness.
garding speaker similarity, all the models we tested showed a better
SMOS compared to the ground truth, a phenomenon also observed in
NaturalSpeech 3 [15].8 Among the tested systems, E2 TTS achieved
a comparable SMOS to Voicebox and NaturalSpeech 3.
Overall, E2 TTS demonstrated a robust zero-shot TTS capabil-
ity that is either superior or comparable to strong baselines, including
Voicebox and NaturalSpeech 3. The comparison between Voicebox
and E2 TTS revealed that the use of phoneme alignment was the pri-
mary obstacle in achieving natural-sounding audio.
